versions.request: Upgrade existing facilities for the homeless
versions.explanation: Every facility must be equipped with Wi-Fi. We fully support this request.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: DHS shares the goal that every shelter should have reliable Wi-Fi. In practice, this can be challenging, as some of our facilities are quite old and not well suited for Wi-Fi installation due to building construction or connectivity limitations (e.g., thick cement walls). That said, all families with children sites either have Wi-Fi or are actively in the queue to receive it. For single adult and adult family (AF) sites, Wi-Fi is not currently a requirement; however, many of these shelters do provide Wi-Fi in common areas, and some also offer computer labs. For sites that do not have on-site Wi-Fi, we work to ensure that clients are informed about where and how they can access Wi-Fi as needed. DHS remains open to ongoing conversations about additional ways to expand and improve Wi-Fi access.

versions.request: New equipment for maintenance
versions.explanation: Bronx Community Board #10 is asking that the City allocate an additional $1 million toward tree pruning in the Bronx.
versions.response: Agency does not support and cannot accommodate Explanation: Parks’ block pruning program provides neighborhood-based, proactive tree maintenance by addressing a portion of the street trees in each CB every year. Parks inspects, then prunes all city-owned street trees above 4" in diameter on a routine 7-year cycle, which is an industry standard. If there are individual trees in need of pruning for public safety, we encourage anyone to submit a service request by locating the tree on the NYC Tree Map (and clicking on the “report a problem” tab), calling 311, or using our online tree service request system. Our inspectors will visit the tree and determine the appropriate action in accordance with our Tree Risk Management program.

versions.request: Other expense budget request for EDC
versions.explanation: We ask that EDC study ways to create a ferry service to City Island and/or Orchard Beach.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: In November 2025, NYCEDC announced a finalized comprehensive redesign of NYC Ferry routes, informed by the proposed map released in the July 2025 Ferry Optimization Plan and shaped by months of stakeholder engagement and public feedback. This redesign reflects a data-driven approach to improving reliability, connectivity, and long-term system sustainability. Looking ahead, NYCEDC plans to engage in a visioning process that considers the broader passenger ferry ecosystem across the New York Harbor beyond NYC Ferry. This future work will include consideration of potential new routes and connections, required landside and waterside infrastructure investments, and the integration of emission-reducing and zero-emission technologies as they become feasible. We encourage Bronx Community Board 10 to review the 2025 NYC Ferry Report for additional detail regarding known issues affecting potential ferry service to City Island that will be revisited and further explored in the visioning process (see page 22). https://edc.nyc/sites/default/files/2025-11/NYCEDC-NYC-Ferry-Report-2025.pdf
